chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, that Ali (peace be upon him) said:
Whoever acknowledges a child and then repudiates him, he is given the flogging (for paternity dispute) and is compelled to provide for the child.

key_terms.جُلِدَ الحَدَّ: He was flogged (with the hadd punishment)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal consequence if a man acknowledges a child and then repudiates him?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, establishing that a man who acknowledges paternity and then repudiates it is subject to the hadd punishment for *al-jud* (disputing paternity) and remains liable for the child's maintenance. This principle underscores the permanence of the *iqrar* (acknowledgment) in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring that the child's right to lineage and financial support is secured even if the father later attempts to disown him.
